root_cause: The implementation is correct (compile, integrity, analyzer, sanitizer tests and CBMC all pass), but Frama-C/WP cannot prove anything about the loop of index_of_max: without a loop invariant WP only knows the loop condition, so the post-conditions in_bounds / is_max / is_first, the runtime-error guards on a[i] and a[best] (mem_access, pointer_value) and 'assigns \nothing' (the loop has no 'loop assigns', so WP assumes it may write everything) stay unproved. Termination is also unproved (no loop variant).
rationale: Proof repair, first step: state the index bounds the loop maintains (1 <= i <= n, 0 <= best < i) and what it writes (loop assigns i, best). These invariants are proof obligations (WP must show they hold initially and are preserved); with them the memory-access and pointer guards, in_bounds and the frame condition become provable. The functional properties is_max / is_first need stronger invariants (next round). No executable code is changed.
